title: Sustained macroscopic quantum coherence in a superradiant solid under ambient conditions
authors: Wei-Jiang Wu, Da-Wu Xiao, Wen-Tao Wang, Xin-Yu Chen, Xian-Feng Wang, Ming-Zhong Ai, Quan Li, Ren-Bao Liu
abstract: Macroscopic quantum coherence, such as in laser, Bose-Einstein condensates, superfluids, and superconductors, is important to fundamental physics and useful for quantum technologies. Superradiance provides a mechanism to produce coherence among a large number of particles and photons. Its implementation, however, has been limited to gaseous systems, solids at very low temperature, or short pulses. Here we demonstrate a solid-state superradiant maser under ambient conditions, which establishes long-lived coherence among about $10^{14}$ nitrogen-vacancy center spins in diamond and about $10^9$ photons in a microwave cavity. By varying the system parameters to access the above-threshold, well-above-threshold, and deep-above-threshold regimes, we observed continuous-wave masing, periodic amplitude modulation, and sequences of superradiant bursts, which are attributed, correspondingly, to macroscopic spin coherence synchronized at a fixed frequency, a coherent time crystal of large spins, and unsynchronized superradiant transients. This work demonstrates that macroscopic quantum coherence can be spontaneously generated and maintained in solids under ambient conditions and provides a solid-state platform for exploring bright quantum lights with many-body correlations.
summary: This paper reports on achieving and characterizing sustained macroscopic quantum coherence in a superradiant solid using NV centers in diamond. By tuning system parameters, the authors observe distinct superradiant regimes—including continuous-wave, periodically modulated, and burst dynamics—confirming the solid-state generation of quantum light with many-body correlations. This establishes a robust platform for quantum technology research.
main_problem: The research aims to demonstrate and characterize sustained macroscopic quantum coherence in a superradiant solid operating under ambient conditions, overcoming limitations previously confining such phenomena to cryogenic or gaseous systems.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated spontaneous generation and maintenance of macroscopic quantum coherence in NV-center spins in diamond, observing distinct superradiant regimes (CW, PAM, bursts) that confirm solid-state quantum light sources.
method: The study combines experimental measurements (microwave spectroscopy, time-domain signal recording) with theoretical modeling using mean-field theory and rate equations to analyze the spin-photon dynamics.
model_or_system: The physical system is a superradiant maser utilizing Nitrogen-Vacancy (NV) center spins in diamond coupled to a microwave cavity. The dynamics are governed by a Hamiltonian describing the interaction between the collective spin ensemble and the cavity field.
key_observables: Continuous-wave (CW) maser emission, periodically amplitude-modulated (PAM) maser oscillations (suggesting a time crystal), and superradiant bursts, alongside coherence decay times.
important_parameters: Cavity linewidth ($\kappa_c$), spin relaxation rates ($\gamma, \sigma, \gamma_\phi$), and the pumping rate ($W$) are key parameters used to access different operational regimes.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mean-field approximations for the collective spin dynamics, and later sections investigate the robustness of coherence against thermal noise.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the experimental setup, the spectral evolution across different pump rates, time-domain signal decay showing long-lived coherence, and Bloch sphere trajectories mapping the system's state in the three distinct operational regimes.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the physical platform and Hamiltonian, detailing the experimental measurements across different pumping regimes (CW, PAM, Burst), and finally analyzing the underlying quantum dynamics, including the effects of thermal noise on coherence persistence.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it provides a solid-state, ambient-condition platform to study fundamental quantum phenomena like superradiance and time-crystalline order, bridging quantum optics with solid-state physics.
